artifacts.summary: Research on making claude-refresh.sh's memory accounting VmSwap-aware: a PROC_ROOT-overridable get_vmswap_kb() helper beside format_memory(), threading combined RSS+swap through all accumulators/display, an invariant ruling that a post-classification /proc read does not breach the snapshot race-freedom argument, and new matcher test cases.

memory_candidates.content: Shell script testability pattern: when a function under test needs to read from a system path that varies at runtime (e.g. /proc/PID/status), use a plain environment-overridable path variable (e.g. PROC_ROOT="${PROC_ROOT:-/proc}") as the seam rather than wrapping the read in a function-override seam. This is lighter-weight than a function-seam (like claude-refresh.sh's existing _pid_is_alive override for kill -0) and sufficient when only a path, not a syscall, needs to be redirected. Tests point the variable at a mktemp -d fixture directory built with inline heredocs (e.g. $WORKDIR/fakeproc/<pid>/status), never at the live /proc tree.

When adding a per-candidate live read (e.g. /proc/PID/status) to a script whose header documents a single-atomic-snapshot race-freedom argument, the read does not breach that invariant IF it is reporting-only (never gates the active/orphan/exclusion decision) and is performed strictly after classification, failing closed (e.g. to 0) rather than erroring when the target has since exited. This distinction (decision-gating live re-query vs. post-decision reporting-only read) should be recorded explicitly in the header comment, not silently assumed, whenever such a read is added.
